extracted.intended_audience: journalists, local news leaders, media researchers, policymakers, and funders interested in public trust in local media
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing public perceptions of local news organizations along trust-related dimensions (accuracy, relevancy, transparency, bias, localness) and implications for editorial choices. The page summarizes survey findings and recommendations about how local outlets can maintain or build trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performing democratic roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news media help keep residents informed of the significant issues facing their cities, towns and nearby areas; hold political and civic leaders accountable for their actions; and foster a sense of community among their readers and viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report frames local news as a 'cornerstone of democracy' — evaluation should consider how well an outlet informs residents, holds leaders accountable, and fosters community cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of most important local issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Americans assess local coverage of most important local issues positively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether coverage addresses the issues residents view as most important and whether that coverage is seen as adequate and relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevancy is a trust dimension where local organizations receive stronger ratings than national organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether reporting is perceived as relevant to the local community's needs and concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency is a trust dimension in which local news generally outperforms national media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess practices that signal openness (e.g., sourcing, corrections, disclosure of conflicts) that contribute to perceived transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / Getting the facts right
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to 'get the facts right' is a central trust dimension; partisan gaps are especially wide on this measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate factual accuracy, fact-checking practices, and perceptions of accuracy across partisan groups; note that Democrats and Republicans differ notably in trust here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived bias and perceived shifts in bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceptions that local news has become more biased (and direction of that shift) strongly affect trust; those who see a shift are about half as likely to trust local news as those who do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both whether audiences perceive bias and the perceived direction (e.g., toward liberal views); perception of increased bias is a major predictor of reduced trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political alignment with the local community
rubrics_metrics.description: People generally see local media as 'in step with, rather than at odds with, the political leanings of their local community.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider how well an outlet's coverage aligns with local political culture and whether perceived alignment affects credibility and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of polarization from covering national/social political issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Moving into more aggressive coverage of social and political issues could further polarize views — and possibly lead to an erosion of trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the civic imperative to cover important political/social topics against the risk that such coverage may be perceived as partisan and reduce trust among segments of the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with nonpartisan local topics (localness of content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local news may have built a trust advantage by being associated with reporting largely nonpartisan topics like local business development, crime, cultural events, the weather and sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track topical mix — emphasis on clearly local, nonpolitical reporting (business, crime, events, weather, sports) appears to support trust; outlets can increase focus on local content to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative trust advantage over national media (contextual skepticism)
rubrics_metrics.description: While local news organizations receive stronger ratings than national organizations across most trust dimensions, this 'trust advantage' may reflect skepticism toward national media rather than strong enthusiasm for local outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret higher local-news trust scores in context: distinguish whether they represent positive assessments of local journalism or primarily lower trust in national outlets.
